items.action: Disable IBE if unused; block internet access to the FortiMail management interface or restrict it to trusted networks. Hunt for the published indicators: new files /data/lib/liblog.so, /data/bin/webconsole, /data/bin/mailservice; modified /data/etc/ld.so.preload, /bin/smit, /data/etc/httpd.conf; and IPs 79.141.169.187 and 45.129.0.192.
items.details: CVSS 9.8 (CWE-22 path traversal + CWE-158 null-byte). Affects FortiMail 7.2.0–7.2.9, 7.4.0–7.4.8, 7.6.0–7.6.6 and 8.0.0–8.0.1. Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-26-175 on October 1, 2026; fixes (8.0.2, 7.6.7, 7.4.9) are still pending, and 7.2 users are told to move to 7.4+. CISA added it to KEV the same day, with federal remediation due October 4 (today).
items.summary: Fortinet says CVE-2026-104286 is being exploited in the wild and no fixed build exists yet. The unauthenticated flaw lets attackers write arbitrary files to the appliance via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests, potentially leading to code execution.
items.title: FortiMail zero-day (CVE-2026-104286) actively exploited, no patch yet

items.action: Upgrade to the fixed release for your train (20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1, 26.2.1); earlier than 20.9 must migrate. Isolate the Manager from the internet. Audit serviceproxy-access.log and vmanage-server.log for URL-encoded j_security_check requests and activity from viptela-reserved- accounts — assume full SD-WAN compromise if found.
items.details: Advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU (Sept 30, 2026). CWE-177 improper URI-encoding handling lets an unauthenticated remote attacker reach the API as the admin user, gaining the netadmin role over the entire SD-WAN fabric. There are no workarounds; Cisco's managed cloud is already patched (20.15.605). CISA KEV-listed Sept 30 with forensic triage required.
items.summary: Cisco patched an authentication bypass in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that is already being exploited. An unauthenticated attacker can gain full admin control of the management plane — and through it, the whole SD-WAN fabric.
items.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day (CVE-2026-76504) exploited in the wild

items.action: Review Moxa advisory MPSA-269540 and apply the published firmware/software updates to affected protocol gateways; restrict management-interface access to trusted networks.
items.details: CVE-2026-86325: stack-based buffer overflow in the account management interface via a crafted account_name, exploitable by an authenticated read-only web user to read credentials from memory, corrupt memory, or disrupt availability. CVE-2026-86326: devices fail to verify firmware image signatures before installation, letting a privileged attacker install modified firmware and persist across updates.
items.summary: Moxa's October 2 advisory MPSA-269540 discloses a buffer overflow and a missing firmware-signature check in its protocol gateways. Apply the fixes now, especially on internet-exposed gateways.
items.title: Moxa discloses two high-severity flaws in protocol gateways (CVE-2026-86325/86326)

items.action: If KillSec listed your organization, confirm scope from the seized data (now in police hands), preserve evidence, and bring in legal and IR — the leak site's victim list is now law-enforcement evidence.
items.details: Led by Hamburg police with Europol/Eurojust, Operation KillSwitch seized five central servers and secured at least 110 terabytes of data. Suspects: a 16-year-old Romanian national detained in Alicante, Spain (suspected main operator), plus two men in their 20s arrested in the U.K. and Romania. KillSec's entry points were software vulnerabilities, poorly secured cloud storage, and credentials bought on the dark web.
items.summary: Europol and Eurojust announced Operation KillSwitch on October 1: the KillSec leak site is in police hands, five servers seized, and three suspects arrested — including a 16-year-old believed to be the group's main operator. About 1,000 suspected attacks worldwide, roughly 500 confirmed successful.
items.title: Police dismantle KillSec ransomware operation; 16-year-old suspected operator arrested

items.details: Claim published on the Wallstreet dark-web leak site and reported October 3; the claim alone does not independently confirm encryption or data exfiltration. St. Francis Healthcare System of Hawai'i is a Catholic nonprofit serving Hawai'i families since 1927.
items.summary: The Wallstreet ransomware group listed St. Francis Healthcare Systems of Hawaii on its leak site on October 3, 2026. Healthcare providers remain a top ransomware target this year.
items.title: Wallstreet ransomware claims St. Francis Healthcare Systems of Hawaii

items.details: Source record: ransomware.live, via cyberthreatintelligence.net (updated Oct 4, 2026). Listed materials reportedly include ~40 scans of Lebanese national ID cards, a director's passport, Byblos Bank employee account files, Cedrus Bank corporate-card program data, and payroll records. Leak-site listing dates reflect disclosure, not the original intrusion.
items.summary: Rhysida listed Lebanon's Skaff Group — a decorative-fabrics leader — on its leak site October 3. The group claims ~268 GB of files including full HR dossiers and banking data.
items.title: Rhysida lists Lebanon's Skaff Group with ~268 GB of data

items.action: Update iPhone, iPad and Mac to the latest iOS, iPadOS and macOS releases immediately; CERT-In urges all users on affected versions to patch.
items.details: CERT-In's October 1 high-severity warning covers iOS, iPadOS and macOS. Apple acknowledges the flaw 'may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals' on versions before iOS 27.
items.summary: CERT-In issued a critical alert for Apple users in India over CVE-2026-86950, warning the vulnerability is already being exploited in targeted, highly sophisticated attacks. Older software versions are at the highest risk.
items.title: CERT-In warns Apple users of actively exploited vulnerability (CVE-2026-86950)

items.details: Other October 3 developments from the same roundup: a Surat mule account linked to 37 cybercrime complaints and about ₹7 crore in alleged fraud, a ₹4.72-crore crypto-investment scam in Gurugram, ₹36.23 crore in cyberfraud losses recorded in Coimbatore over nine months, and UP reporting ₹874.58 crore in cybercrime money frozen or put on hold.
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate uncovered a ₹734-crore fake-GST-credit network built around 135 shell companies, among 10 major cybercrime developments reported on October 3 — from crypto-investment scams to mule-account networks.
items.title: ED uncovers ₹734-crore fake GST credit network across 135 shell companies
